record.prompt: Write a story about a homeowner who’s spent twelve years pulling invasive, poisonous plants from their garden after discovering they were planted by the previous owner, a self-professed witch. Start your story on the day they uncover a hidden sprig of belladonna under the porch and stumble on an old grimoire of toxic herbs. End with the moment they hand over the keys to the new owners along with a heartfelt letter revealing everything. Include a near-tragic mishap, a debate over legal and moral obligations to disclose, and the weight of keeping—or sharing—dangerous secrets. The finished story should be roughly 8,000–10,000 words.

Hey, can you write a story about someone who keeps having the same dream of a dense forest bathed in a purple-green glow? Start with them stepping under the towering trees and following the light to a massive ancient tree where a levitating crystal covered in shifting runes waits in its roots. End with the moment they finally discover what the crystal means and how it changes their waking life forever. Make sure to include vivid descriptions of the forest atmosphere, the eerie runes, at least two flashback scenes to earlier dreams, and a strong sense of destiny. The story should be roughly 8,000-10,000 words.

Pick up where this story left off and follow Peter as he wakes inside a dim, rattling wagon with a hood over his head. Show his first moments of fear and confusion as the horses carry him through a devastated landscape, then introduce the strangers who capture him and his attempts to bridge the language barrier. Explore how he deciphers their intentions, whether they seek to exploit his ageless condition or protect him, and how this encounter reshapes his quest for answers. The completed story should be 12,000-15,000 words.

Pick up where this story left off: Detective Schroeder sits alone in his cell, determined to prove he didn’t kill his daughter. As he uncovers evidence of a conspiracy led by Commissioner Gaider and his own partner, he must form an uneasy alliance with a sympathetic jail guard and hack into police records to find the truth. Include at least three flashback scenes to Stephanie’s last day, a daring break-in to retrieve hidden CCTV footage, and a tense courtroom finale. The finished story should run 12,000-15,000 words.

Write a fun, conversational story of about 8,000–10,000 words based on this idea: a petite woman keeps pace drink-for-drink with her big former college buddy in a lakeside cabin, blacking out and later yelling “the bench fell over” hours before it actually does. Dive into her hazy memories, playful group dynamics, and the eerie possibility that she’s psychic when blackout drunk. Set the scene in a misty, rustic cabin, include a couple of flashbacks to college pranks, weave in comedic chaos and mounting tension, and explore her unreliable narration. Make sure to highlight her inner doubts, build suspense leading up to the “vision,” and end with a surprising twist about what really happened.

Turn this movie idea into a full 8,000–10,000-word story about the Ghostbusters reuniting to battle a river of psychomagnetic slime under Manhattan and an evil 17th-century tyrant trapped in a painting. Start with Dana Barrett’s frantic buggy chase and build up to the courtroom clash, a creepy haunted birthday party, and the climactic rescue of her baby, ending with the team calling on the Statue of Liberty to save New York. Make sure your narrative balances sharp humor with supernatural thrills, deepens the bonds between the four Ghostbusters and Dana, and weaves in an unexpected twist around ancient prophecy. Keep the pacing brisk, the banter snappy, and let the city itself feel like another character in your thrilling ghost story.

Create an original story about a village where every child’s name foretells the life they’ll lead and follow the case of a girl fated to “Consume Flames.” Show the weight of expectation on her parents, the townsfolk’s fear, and her own struggle to carve out a different future. Include at least two key scenes: one where the villagers confront her family, and another where she must face her destiny head-on. Focus on themes of free will versus fate, societal prejudice, and the strength of familial love, and write 10,000-13,000 words.

Invent a tale about the last refuge of humanity deep beneath a ruined city, where survivors convert medieval escape tunnels into a modern war bunker for one final stand against an alien invasion. Focus on themes of defiance, sacrifice, and the thin line between hope and despair as a lone sergeant mans a jury-rigged autocannon against overwhelming odds. Include four key scenes: scavenging ancient traps in the catacombs, training terrified civilians as militia, the siege at the tunnels’ choke point, and the sergeant’s haunting flashback to a fallen comrade. The story should be 10,000-13,000 words.

Write a roughly 8,000–10,000 word story about a young guy who grew up in Detroit and learned never to judge a book by its cover but always stay ready to defend himself. Start your story the moment he steps off a bus in New York, recalling the night his dad showed him how to turn household items into weapons. End with him facing a would-be mugger on a city street and deciding between violence and understanding. Include at least two flashbacks to Detroit’s struggling neighborhoods, show his internal conflict over first impressions, and weave in the theme that everyone has a backstory you don’t see at first glance.

Write a story about two exes who decide to remain close friends after their breakup. Start your story with them feeling the awkward tension at a mutual friend’s house party the night they end things, and end it with both of them happily on a double date with new partners. Include honest dialogues showing their fears and honest acceptance, moments of reflection on forgiveness and growth, and scenes where they give each other relationship advice. Explore themes of friendship after romance, personal growth, and the unexpected bonds that endure. The story should be around 8,000 to 10,000 words.

Write a story about an older brother who can’t help but judge his younger sister’s bizarre TV obsessions. Start with him freaking out over her comments about witches and midgets in a daytime soap, then follow him as she turns the tables by asking about his Star Trek marathon. End with the two of them side by side on the couch, her teasing his outlandish theories and them sharing a knowing, silent nod. Include at least two major misunderstandings, a childhood prank flashback, and a warm sibling bond threading through every scene. The finished story should be roughly 8,000–10,000 words.

Continue this story: A veteran private investigator is called to the Nijō family’s corporate headquarters after a series of untraceable accounting adjustments threaten their century-old confectionery business. As she examines hidden ledgers, half-erased memos and late-night security logs, she uncovers subtle inconsistencies that point toward a beloved family member and a buried ethical scandal. Guide the narrative with methodical deductions and logical pacing in the style of Keigo Higashino, include at least three surprising but plausible twists rooted in family loyalty and corporate intrigue, and deliver a complete short story of 8,000–12,000 words.

Continue the story about someone with crippling stage fright who vows to face their fears after a chat with their game dev tutor. Start at the moment they walk on stage for that department presentation, laying out their racing thoughts and sweaty palms, then show how they draw on the tutor’s advice to turn things around. Weave in details about challenges—maybe a sudden tech glitch or an unexpected question from the audience—and flashbacks to past embarrassments. Build it into a roughly 8,000-10,000 word narrative about growth, performance, and the power of pushing past fear.

Pick up where this story left off: with coffee finally in his grasp, the familiar warmth of the cup ignites more than just his senses—he unwittingly cracks open a veil between realities. As the line disperses and the city seems unchanged, subtle rifts in the sky and whispers in the air hint at the ancient terrors now unbound. Follow his desperate journey to undo what he’s unleashed and examine the sacrifices he must make for love, weaving in at least two violent confrontations and one moment of tragic redemption. The final narrative should be 9,000-11,000 words.

Expand this concept into a full story: a lifelong atheist dies and awakens in a boundless white room before a finely dressed figure claiming to be God, who challenges them with the question “Did you live well?” Explore the protagonist’s life through three pivotal flashbacks—family moments, career choices, and a moral dilemma—and show how these shape their understanding of happiness, purpose, and faith. Weave introspective narration with vivid sensory details and dynamic dialogue, building tension in each encounter until the final step into the unknown. Target length: 10,000–15,000 words.

Write a detailed story based on this idea: in a small Midwestern farming town a few rich families keep thousands of cattle in barns all winter and then let pigs loose on the thick layer of manure instead of buying grain. The main character is a young farmhand who discovers this cost-cutting scheme and struggles with loyalty to his boss, his own moral code, and the need to support his family. Set the narrative over a full year with vivid descriptions of the seasons, the smells and sounds of the barns, and the daily grind of farm life. Make sure to explore themes of greed, community pressure, and personal growth and aim for roughly 8,000 to 10,000 words.

Write a roughly 8,000–10,000 word story based on this setup: you’re a small-time hustler who takes your boss’s wife out for a night on the town, only to have her mistake your heroin for coke and start overdosing. Flesh out the narrator, the boss’s wife, and the street dealer, and show how their backstories and motivations collide. Set the action in a gritty, neon-lit cityscape, build tension as you rush to save her with adrenaline, and explore themes of trust, desperation, and survival. Make sure to include vivid sensory details and a moral twist that leaves readers questioning who’s really in control.

Imagine a world where everyone carries a secret death-phrase tattooed on their wrist and can only truly die when their soul mate whispers it aloud. Create an original thriller about a renegade archaeologist who uncovers an ancient prophecy linking these phrases to the collapse of empires and is forced to protect the woman she loves from foes who want her words for themselves. Explore themes of destiny versus choice, the burdens of eternal life, and the redemptive power of love. Aim for 10,000–14,000 words.

Imagine a rainy jungle valley where a young shepherd’s only water buffalo is stolen by a cunning jackal. In desperation she prays at a hidden shrine and is summoned before a luminous phoenix-eagle aflame with golden wings. The bird offers one glowing feather that grants a single selfless wish—but warns her that greed will undo her heart’s desire. Explore themes of faith, trust, and compassion in this 12,000-15,000 word tale.

Write a new story about a city that survived a catastrophic viral outbreak only to have its government secretly erase everyone’s memories to enforce order—except for one high school teacher whose mind remains intact. Explore her grief for lost students, her discovery of an underground data archive, and her tense alliance with a rogue AI companion to expose the truth. Include two rival factions vying for control, a hidden ritual that can restore suppressed memories at great risk, and a final showdown in an abandoned subway station. The tale should be between 10,000 and 14,000 words.
